units.content: Decide whether every efficiently verifiable decision problem is also efficiently solvable, equivalently whether SAT has a polynomial-time algorithm.
units.title: P vs NP

units.content: Cook and Karp show that many apparently different problems are interreducible through polynomial reductions and share SAT as a complete core. What remained open: Completeness explains universality of difficulty but not the source of lower bounds against all polynomial-time algorithms or circuits.
units.title: 1971-1972: Verification becomes a universal computational phenomenon

units.content: Relativization shows that any proof surviving arbitrary oracle substitution cannot settle the main question. What remained open: The barrier diagnoses broad method families but does not identify a successful nonrelativizing replacement.
units.title: 1975: Proof techniques become objects of study

units.content: Algebraic, proof-complexity, descriptive, and structural viewpoints re-express computation through polynomials, proofs, reductions, and uniformity conditions. What remained open: Every translation risks losing target strength: a theorem in a restricted or algebraic model must still return to Boolean P vs NP or P/poly with controlled loss.
units.title: Late 1970s onward: Complexity becomes a landscape of representations

units.content: Natural proofs explain why many broad, efficiently checkable combinatorial properties are unlikely to prove strong unrestricted circuit lower bounds. What remained open: The field still needs useful lower-bound properties that are either not large, not constructive, not black-box, or otherwise outside the natural-proofs template.
units.title: 1990s: Lower-bound intuitions meet pseudorandomness

units.content: Hardness transfers are judged by exact exponents, target-query counts, advice leakage, and whether a weak source lower bound really magnifies to the main target. What remained open: Most bridges lose too much exponent, import nonuniform advice, or prove a source lower bound that is already as hard as the desired conclusion.
units.title: 2000s onward: Fine-grained and magnification thinking exposes exponent debt

units.content: Algebrization and restricted-circuit lower bounds clarify both the reach and limits of current techniques. What remained open: The unrestricted P vs NP question still demands a target-preserving lower bound or impossibility theorem that escapes known barriers without losing the main quantifiers.
units.title: 2009 onward: Modern progress is real but carefully scoped

units.content: The Complexity of Theorem-Proving Procedures. Supports: Introduces NP-completeness through satisfiability and turns efficient verification into a universal problem.. Limitation: It defines the central complete problem and reduction method; it does not separate deterministic from nondeterministic polynomial time.
units.title: ref.cook-1971

units.content: Reducibility Among Combinatorial Problems. Supports: Shows that many natural search and optimization problems share the same NP-complete core.. Limitation: NP-completeness transfers difficulty conditionally; it does not prove that any NP-complete problem lacks polynomial algorithms.
units.title: ref.karp-1972

units.content: Relativizations of the P = ? NP Question. Supports: Shows that relativizing methods alone cannot settle P vs NP, because oracle worlds exist on both sides.. Limitation: Relativization is a diagnostic for proof techniques, not a proof that separation is impossible.
units.title: ref.baker-gill-solovay-1975

units.content: Natural Proofs. Supports: Explains why many combinatorial lower-bound properties are too large and constructive to prove strong general circuit lower bounds under cryptographic hardness assumptions.. Limitation: The barrier constrains a proof format; it leaves room for non-natural, nonconstructive, algebraic, or otherwise barrier-evading arguments.
units.title: ref.razborov-rudich-1997

units.content: Algebrization: A New Barrier in Complexity Theory. Supports: Shows that even many non-relativizing arithmetization methods still fall inside an algebrizing barrier.. Limitation: Algebrization does not rule out all algebraic or geometric methods; it forces proof attempts to state exactly what escapes the barrier.
units.title: ref.aaronson-wigderson-2009

units.content: Which Problems Have Strongly Exponential Complexity?. Supports: Develops reduction notions that preserve subexponential complexity and clarify how quantitative hardness transfers.. Limitation: Strong exponential-time hypotheses and SERF reductions illuminate hardness structure but do not by themselves separate P from NP.
units.title: ref.impagliazzo-paturi-zane-2001

units.content: Nonuniform ACC Circuit Lower Bounds. Supports: Proves that NEXP does not have polynomial-size nonuniform ACC circuits and demonstrates an algorithms-to-lower-bounds bridge.. Limitation: The result is a major restricted-circuit breakthrough, not a lower bound against unrestricted polynomial-size circuits for NP.
units.title: ref.williams-2014

units.content: Completeness Classes in Algebra. Supports: Creates an algebraic analogue of completeness and lower-bound questions, showing how representation and computation can be studied through polynomial families.. Limitation: Algebraic complexity gives powerful analogues and transfer pressure, but VP vs VNP is not literally the Boolean P vs NP problem.
units.title: ref.valiant-1979

units.title: main_problem_alignment

units.content: The exact quantitative transfer is C(Pad_k(SAT)_N)<=O(N+N^{c/k}); hence the barely-superlinear lower bound magnifies only up to target exponent k(1+epsilon). The valid bridge is useful as an exponent-calibrated route lemma, while the fixed-k P/poly claim is blocked by a concrete threshold falsifier rather than by vague folklore. Next: Instantiate the same exponent audit for a padded MKtP or GapMCSP carrier: name the verifier, compute Cook-Levin or direct-composition length blow-up, and test whether assuming SAT in SIZE(n^c) yields source circuits below N^{1+epsilon} without model mismatch or nonuniform leakage.
units.title: cycle-0001: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 2 turns the previous threshold collapse into an exact quantifier repair. The valid route lemma is: fixed k gives only a finite SAT exponent lower bound, while a common-epsilon lower bound for unbounded padded carriers H_k would imply NP not subset P/poly. The decisive falsifier is not folklore but the inequality c/k>=1+epsilon, plus the O(N) checker floor. Next: Test MCSP or proof-complexity carriers for producing the unbounded-k source family: formalize whether a weak lower bound for MCSP[2^{N^{1/k}}] transfers to C_{H_k}(N)>N^{1+epsilon} without becoming natural or losing the strict exponent margin.
units.title: cycle-0002: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 3 finds a valid single-carrier repair: growth padding N_m=(m+1)^{g(m+1)} converts an i.o. N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for H_g into exclusion of every SAT exponent c. This is route-level progress, not P vs NP; the hard obligation is now the sparse valid-length lower bound. Next: Instantiate g(r)=ceil(log log(r+4)); prove the verifier and length test are poly(N), then analyze whether valid-slice lower bounds for H_g admit a proof-complexity or MCSP carrier formulation.
units.title: cycle-0003: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 4 proves a valid projection-sandwich lemma and demagnifies the sparse-padding route: N^{1+eps} lower bounds for H_g equal m^{(1+eps)g} SAT lower bounds. The bridge is correct but not a weak-source path toward P vs NP. Next: Test an MCSP or KT-complexity carrier with source model, threshold N^{1+eps}, and target NP not subset P/poly; compute the reduction overhead and state whether the needed proof must be non-natural or non-algebrizing.
units.title: cycle-0004: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 5 converts the padding quarantine into a general projection-carrier dichotomy. The valid bridge says N^{1+epsilon} lower bounds transfer through ell(N) only when ell(N)^c is below the threshold. Positive polynomial embedding length gives only a bounded exponent window; subpolynomial embedding length gives all exponents but turns the source lower bound into ell(N)^{omega(1)}. Thus pure projection magnification fails as a weak-source path, with an explicit falsifier rather than a slogan. Next: Audit an MCSP-based route: set source object MCSP_{n,s} on N=2^n-bit truth tables, choose a concrete circuit model for the lower bound, state the exact threshold N^{1+epsilon} or smaller, and test whether the known magnification transfer is non-natural, target-preserving, and strong enough to imply SAT notin P/poly rather than only EXP or subexponential derandomization consequences.
units.title: cycle-0005: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 6 shows that moving from projection padding to a nonprojection MCSP carrier does not by itself create major magnification. The valid transfer is C(MCSP_{N^alpha},N)<=N^{c(1+alpha)+o(1)} under SAT in SIZE(n^c), so an N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound excludes only c<(1+epsilon)/(1+alpha). The input-reading floor alpha>=0 caps any fixed barely-superlinear bridge below all-exponent P/poly separation. The failure is a concrete threshold falsifier, not barrier folklore. Next: Test a self-referential meta-complexity carrier, such as Gap-MCSP or MKtP with succinctly generated truth tables, where the target SAT circuit is used nonblack-box. Compute whether the induced carrier upper bound can avoid the multiplicative c factor; if not, quarantine it by the same beta-ceiling lemma.
units.title: cycle-0006: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization, Cycle 6: MCSP verifier transfer audit

units.content: Cycle 7 generalizes the MCSP and padding failures to an oracle-interface theorem. A barely-superlinear carrier lower bound transfers through a black-box SAT interface as max{a,q+beta c}; hence positive target-query length exponent beta is the decisive threshold-collapse falsifier. The remaining valid route must either use subpolynomial target queries with a genuinely nonprojection carrier or abandon black-box substitution. Next: Test a succinct local-consistency or proof-complexity carrier with N^{o(1)} SAT queries: compute a,q,beta, then run the projection-demagnification falsifier before claiming any magnification.
units.title: cycle-0007: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: black-box substitution cap

units.content: Cycle 8 repairs the remaining route exactly: subpolynomial SAT-query length is sufficient to remove the c-dependent threshold term, so N^{1+epsilon} lower bounds magnify only when max(a,q)<1+epsilon. The valid contribution is a quantified bridge plus a model-preservation gate; the unresolved hard task is finding a concrete carrier satisfying the interface and source lower bound without natural-proof or nonuniform-leakage failure. Next: Search for non-truth-table carriers in P^SAT with near-linear ordinary work and subpolynomial SAT queries, e.g. succinct consistency or decompression-check problems, then compute A,Q,s and test against L8.1 before discussing P vs NP.
units.title: cycle-0008: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization, cycle 8: subpolynomial-query threshold repair

units.content: Cycle 9 converts the cycle-8 repair into a route failure certificate. Subpolynomial SAT queries remove the c-dependent upper-bound term, but the same transfer read backward says that proving the source N^{1+epsilon} lower bound in general SIZE already proves SAT_{<=L} has L^{omega(1)} circuits lower bounds. The remaining valid work is not carrier search inside this black-box same-model interface; it is either a restricted-model closure theorem or a nonblackbox carrier. Next: Pivot to a nonblackbox object: test a proof-complexity or derandomization carrier where SAT in P/poly yields the required source upper bound through a named nonrelativizing theorem rather than through black-box SAT-query substitution.
units.title: cycle-0009: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: subpolynomial-interface demagnification

units.content: Cycle 10 proves a valid restricted-model closure bridge and names the precise target-preservation failure. Subpolynomial queries plus max(a,q)<1+epsilon magnify a Gamma lower bound to SAT notin Gamma/poly for every fixed exponent. This is real route-level progress, but it is not NP notin P/poly: the missing object is a nonuniform P/poly-to-Gamma lift with subthreshold tax, and its absence is the decisive falsifier for advertising the bridge as a P vs NP route. Next: Test a non-natural nonblackbox carrier whose query length is N^{o(1)} and whose use of a SAT circuit is semantic rather than oracle substitution; compute whether its lift tax delta is below the source slack epsilon.
units.title: cycle-0010: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 11 turns the cycle-10 target split into a sharper impossibility triangle. To lift Gamma lower bounds to P/poly by unrolling arbitrary SAT circuits, queries must be so short that every SAT query can also be answered by unconditional lookup inside Gamma. That gives H_N a subthreshold Gamma upper bound and falsifies the source lower bound. Intermediate log-query lengths either collapse the source or preserve only exponent c<=1. Thus black-box formula-style P/poly repair is quarantined; progress now requires a genuinely nonblackbox carrier or a proof object where target circuits are used without independent short-query lookup. Next: Test a nonblackbox proof-complexity carrier: encode a SAT circuit as a verifier object whose correctness is checked globally rather than by short oracle leaves, and compute whether the verifier overhead stays below N^{1+epsilon} without allowing SAT_{<=L} truth-table substitution.
units.title: cycle-0011: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: lookup-lift collapse for restricted target repair

units.content: Cycle 12 identifies a real surviving window: superlogarithmic subpolynomial target lengths, especially L=(log N)^d with d>1. In this window SAT circuits of size L^c amortize to N^{o(1)}, but SAT truth tables cost 2^L and no longer give the old subthreshold lookup falsifier. The bridge is valid only for nonblackbox compact-circuit consumers; it is not a P vs NP proof without the explicit carrier and lower bound. Next: Instantiate H_N as a proof-checking or self-reduction transcript language whose verifier can call a compact SAT_L circuit nonblackbox; compute its exact overhead a and test whether full truth-table substitution or input-encoded D leakage gives a subthreshold upper bound.
units.title: cycle-0012: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 13 turns the superlogarithmic polylog window into an exact bridge: L=(log N)^d with d>1 makes SAT circuits of size L^c amortize to N^{o(1)}, while truth-table lookup costs 2^L=N^{omega(1)} and no longer supplies the old falsifier. The valid threshold is rho<1+epsilon for a target-clean nonblackbox compact consumer. The new hard obstruction is not folklore but the absence of an explicit carrier with no advice leakage and a non-natural N^{1+epsilon} general-circuit lower bound. Next: Instantiate PolyLogAudit_{N,d,V} with a universal-circuit verifier, compute the exact overhead exponent rho and auxiliary advice length, and reject the instance immediately if H_N depends on a hidden SAT circuit or collapses to a black-box SAT query family.
units.title: cycle-0013: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: Polylog Nonblackbox Compact Consumer

units.content: Cycle 14 identifies a concrete carrier template, H_N=OR of N^q generated SAT instances of length (log N)^d, and computes the exact transfer: SAT in SIZE(n^c) gives H_N in SIZE(N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}). The valid magnification window is max{rho,q}<1+epsilon plus lookup safety N^rho+N^q2^L not subthreshold. For d>1, exhaustive lookup is N^{q+omega(1)}, so the previous short-query falsifier is avoided, but the source lower bound remains the hard non-natural obligation. Next: Instantiate G_N as a near-linear Cook-Levin micro-instance generator with M=N and L=(log N)^d; compute exact rho, verify H_N is in NP with poly(N) uniform verification, and test whether any structural simplification gives an N^{1+epsilon} upper-bound falsifier.
units.title: cycle-0014: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: polylog generated-OR carrier

units.content: Cycle 15 adds the exact lookup boundary. Polylog queries always preserve all SAT polynomial exponents in the substitution term, but source plausibility requires q+A(log N)^{d-1} not fall below 1+epsilon. Thus d<1 is quarantined, d=1 has a sharp constant window, and d>1 is safely valid from lookup. Next: Instantiate the boundary cases d=1 with A=1+epsilon-q and d=2; search for a generator whose H_N avoids known small-circuit constructions without smuggling SAT advice.
units.title: cycle-0015: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 16 sharpens the generated-OR route: the valid transfer to SAT notin P/poly needs only q,rho<1+epsilon, but source plausibility additionally requires variable entropy q+v/log N at least 1+epsilon. The old 2^L lookup audit was too weak; the real falsifier is low variable count. Low variable count or low positioned range is a concrete falsifier, not a folklore barrier. Subthreshold S_N is a concrete falsifier for H_N lower bounds, while q,rho<1+epsilon still gives the target-preserving implication from a valid H_N lower bound to SAT notin P/poly. units.content: Cycle 20 sharpens the generated-OR route: the valid target bridge is unchanged, but the source plausibility gate must minimize over semantic block covers. Singleton range complexity is too weak because OR compression and nonuniform block advice can falsify an N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound. This is route-level progress, not a proof of P != NP. The new quantitative obstruction is T_N>N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)} for SAT restricted to U_N, plus the earlier semantic block-cover threshold. This is route-level progress, not a proof of P != NP. units.content: Cycle 23 adds an exact range-label balance gate. Even with q,rho in the valid target window, a generated-OR carrier is source-plausible only if both satisfiable and unsatisfiable parts of its actual generated range exceed N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)}. This is a concrete falsifier derived from equality-DNF membership circuits, independent of vague barrier folklore. units.title: cycle-0023: Hardness-magnification bridge realization: generated-OR range-balance gate

units.content: Cycle 24 sharpens the generated-OR route from label balance to exact hitting-cover hardness. The valid target bridge is unchanged, but the source lower bound must now defeat nonuniform covers of positive fibers and negative product fibers of total size N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}. This gives a new concrete falsifier and shows that high semantic range entropy alone cannot justify the carrier. Next: Formalize the minimum cover parameter as a bipartite set-cover problem between input fibers and generated SAT labels; test whether known disperser/extractor-style generators can force kappa_N>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} without reintroducing nonuniform leakage.
units.title: cycle-0024: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: hitting-cover gate for generated-OR carriers

units.content: Cycle 25 adds a shared-selector leakage gate. A generated-OR carrier can be easy via one compact selector and a promise SAT solver on only the selected image, even when additive semantic or hitting covers look expensive. Thus the valid source obligation is not merely high range entropy or label balance; it is lower bounding every selector-plus-selected-range-solver pair above N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} while preserving q,rho<1+epsilon for the target bridge. Next: Instantiate Sel_N for simple generator templates, including lexicographic first-satisfying-query generators and hash-bucketed query generators, and compute whether selected-image lookup already drops below N^{1+epsilon}.
units.title: cycle-0025: Generated-OR magnification: selector-range leakage gate

units.content: Cycle 26 adds an approximate-selector gate. Exact witness selection was too weak as a source audit: even a selector wrong on N^{delta} inputs collapses H_N below N^{1+epsilon} when delta<epsilon, because unrestricted circuits correct the errors with equality advice. The valid route obligation is the minimax lower bound Lambda_N>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}, while the clean target bridge q,rho<1+epsilon remains intact. Next: Instantiate the thought experiment with a block generator E_N whose coordinates are grouped into planted easy and hard ranges; compute the smallest delta forced by coverage of positive inputs and test whether selected-range promise SAT stays subthreshold.
units.title: cycle-0026: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 27 upgrades the source audit from approximate single selectors to approximate list selectors. The valid target-preserving bridge is unchanged, but a short list plus a promise solver can decide H_N without computing a canonical witness. Therefore any contribution-making lower-bound attempt must lower-bound Lambda_N^{list}; otherwise the route has a concrete nonuniform-leakage falsifier. Next: Instantiate G_N with a high-entropy expander/hash-generated SAT family and compute whether any tau=O(epsilon/2) list selector has a selected image admitting a subthreshold promise solver.
units.title: cycle-0027: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: approximate list-selector leakage gate

units.content: Cycle 28 identifies an additional leakage mode: many imperfect list selectors can collectively cover the positive fiber. The valid source audit is the ensemble cover complexity Xi_N^{ens}; single-selector minimax lower bounds are insufficient for this generated-OR magnification route. Next: Estimate Xi_N^{ens} for a random high-entropy generator by a union-bound model over ensembles, then isolate which part of the argument can survive explicitness and avoid natural-proof leakage.
units.title: cycle-0028: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 29 sharpens the generated-OR source audit from ensemble list selectors to one-sided selected-image separators. The valid target bridge still needs only q,rho<1+epsilon, but the source lower bound must now beat Psi_N^{sep}; small local labelers are a concrete falsifier even when they do not solve SAT globally. Next: Try to lower-bound or construct Psi_N^{sep} for a random-like generator: estimate whether selected positive and negative images admit N^b-size separators when R=N^r and s=N^ell are below the magnification threshold.
units.title: cycle-0029: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: one-sided separating-ensemble leakage gate

units.content: Cycle 30 replaces the one-sided selected-image audit by the weaker and more dangerous relaxed bag-separator audit. The valid target bridge is unchanged, but the source lower bound must defeat predicates that merely hit one positive witness per positive bag and avoid all negative-bag formulas. This exposes a concrete nonuniform-leakage falsifier not captured by promise SAT hardness. Next: Formalize SepHit_N as a bipartite hitting-avoidance problem between positive bags and negative formula occurrences, then test whether random-looking generators satisfy the required lower bound by a counting argument and where explicitness breaks the argument.
units.title: cycle-0030: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 31 converts relaxed bag separators into an approximate threshold lemma: E bad bags cost NE gates, so errors below N^epsilon are nonuniformly patchable. The valid source obligation is now an approximate distribution-local separator lower bound, not merely promise SAT hardness. Next: Try a collision-balanced generator and estimate whether majority/hash-based local predicates yield s=N^{o(1)} with E<N^epsilon; if yes, quarantine this carrier family.
units.title: cycle-0031: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: approximate relaxed bag separators

units.content: Cycle 32 converts the approximate bag-separator gate into an exact correction-residual gate. The valid target bridge is unchanged, but the source lower bound must prove Phi_N>1+epsilon-o(1): every small local formula predicate must leave a residual H_N xor S_A of high circuit complexity. Sparse error patching is only one falsifier; structured residual leakage is the stronger obstruction. Next: Instantiate Phi_N for a tagged generated-OR carrier and compute whether simple tag predicates produce subthreshold residual circuits; then test an untagged high-entropy generator for the same residual leakage.
units.title: cycle-0032: Generated-OR magnification: correction-residual separator gate

units.content: Cycle 33 strengthens the generated-OR source obligation from single residual correction to feature-aggregator residual hardness. This is a contribution-making repair: it preserves the exact target bridge but exposes a broader nonuniform-leakage falsifier class that prior selector and separator audits did not cover. Next: Formalize the restricted case where B is a depth-2 threshold or DNF over t=N^tau local features, compute the exact q+alpha+beta leakage threshold, and search for an explicit low-residual construction on expander-walk generated SAT bags.
units.title: cycle-0033: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 34 adds a quantitative tuple-arity term to the generated-OR audit. The valid target bridge still needs only max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, but the source lower bound must rule out every subthreshold tuple-feature transcript with exponent s+tq+alpha and residual exponent lambda. This yields a finite dense-arity falsifier search and a sharper nonuniform-leakage obstruction, without claiming P != NP. Next: Instantiate the pair-pattern thought experiment for t=2: choose q with q<1+epsilon and test whether 2q+alpha<1+epsilon permits a subthreshold pair separator S_N; compute the residual complexity C(H_N xor S_N) and check for hidden SAT lookup.
units.title: cycle-0034: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: tuple-feature residual gate

units.content: Cycle 35 finds a parameter repair: set q in ((1+epsilon)/2,1+epsilon) to preserve the generated-OR target bridge while forcing every dense tuple-feature transcript of arity at least two above the N^{1+epsilon} threshold. The route-level lower-bound obligation is now the sharper unary residual minimax gate, not an infinite tuple-arity audit. units.title: cycle-0035: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: high-q arity cutoff for generated-OR carriers

units.content: Cycle 36 repairs the high-q unary reduction: binary and higher tuple features are threshold-blocked when q>(1+epsilon)/2, but shared-unary audits are not sound for general circuits. The valid remaining source obligation is a position-indexed unary transcript plus residual lower bound with total local budget U_N. This is a sharper route-level gate and supplies an explicit falsifier class, without claiming P != NP. units.title: cycle-0036: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: position-indexed unary residual gate

units.content: Cycle 37 sharpens the position-indexed unary residual obligation into an approximate witness-cover threshold. In the high-q generated-OR route, dense tuple leakage is threshold-blocked, but unary assignment covers of total size below N^{1+epsilon} plus fewer than N^epsilon missed positives still give exact circuits for H_N after equality patching. This is route-level progress: a valid candidate source lower bound must first prove high approximate witness-cover complexity, while the main P != NP conjecture remains untouched. units.title: cycle-0037: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: approximate witness-cover gate

units.content: Cycle 38 isolates a canonical unary leakage mechanism: all realized satisfying witnesses per generated position form a zero-error cover. Thus a valid high-q generated-OR route needs W_N^*>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} or a stronger approximate-cover lower bound. The target substitution bridge survives, but source plausibility is now governed by witness-projection entropy rather than formula-range entropy alone. units.title: cycle-0038: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: realized-witness projection gate

units.content: Cycle 39 sharpens the generated-OR source audit: full realized witness entropy is not the right gate because partial satisfying terms can compress many witnesses. The valid target bridge remains max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, but the route now needs a superthreshold lower bound against position-indexed partial-term covers, and ultimately against sound local certificate covers. Next: Formalize tau_N^{term} as a set-cover problem over generated CNF ranges and test whether random-looking high-q generators can force tau_N^{term}>N^{1+epsilon} without making G_N nonexplicit or violating rho<1+epsilon.
units.title: cycle-0039: High-q generated-OR carrier: partial-certificate cover gate

units.content: Cycle 40 sharpens the source audit from partial certificate covers to approximate sound local certificate covers. The exact upper bound C(H_N)<=C(G_N)+O(K(s+L^{O(1)})+EN) makes any subthreshold SLC cover a concrete falsifier. The target bridge remains valid, but a contribution now requires a superthreshold lower bound against one-sided local predicates on the generated range, not just high witness or formula entropy. units.title: cycle-0040: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: sound local certificate cover gate

units.content: Cycle 41 isolates the exact semantic object behind the sound-local-certificate audit: Sep_N^{1s}(E). Random term-cover calculations support the high-q polylog design, but they do not imply the needed separator lower bound. units.title: cycle-0041: One-sided promise-separator gate for high-q generated-OR magnification

units.title: cycle-0044: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: residual cap-denominator gate

units.content: Cycle 45 adds the missing logarithmic greedy-cover charge and converts the cap profile into an exact threshold: D_{sigma,E}<N^{epsilon-sigma-o(1)} is a concrete upper-bound falsifier for the generated-OR source lower bound. units.content: Cycle 46 converts the cycle-45 normal-form warning into a precise obstruction. Greedy cap and separator denominators give valid upper-bound falsifiers, but separator hardness is not by itself a source lower bound. A planted-control generated-OR carrier can have H_N easy while local formula separators remain hard, so the route now needs a nonrelativizing locality-extraction theorem or a direct arbitrary-circuit lower bound for H_N. units.title: cycle-0046: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: normal-form extraction gate

units.content: Cycle 47 converts the locality-extraction warning into a formal relativizing obstruction. A planted-control oracle gives hard one-sided local separators but an O(1)-size generated-OR carrier, so separator hardness is not a valid source lower-bound certificate by itself. units.title: cycle-0047: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: locality-extraction obstruction

units.title: cycle-0048: Relativizing locality-extraction gate for generated-OR carriers

units.content: Cycle 49 converts the surviving generated-OR route into an exact extraction-threshold problem. Separator-denominator hardness is a valid source certificate only if every small H circuit yields covers with denominator S/N^{1+sigma}+N^kappa and kappa<epsilon-sigma. Neutralization gives a concrete extraction but is a demagnifying falsifier, because it asks for restricted-SAT hardness rather than a barely-superlinear H lower bound. units.title: cycle-0049: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: locality extraction threshold

units.title: cycle-0050: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: Relativizing Extraction Falsified

Hence slot-wise SAT hardness cannot be the weak source; a valid route must prove aggregate H_N hardness or supply a nonrelativizing extraction theorem. units.title: cycle-0051: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization - cycle 51 direct-sum demagnification audit

The new source burden is sharper: prove aggregate parity-carrier hardness or rule out subthreshold parity sketches and sparse corrections. This is route-level progress only, with explicit falsifier tests. The carrier equals the F_2 inner product of the SAT label vector with a generated parity-incidence vector; low-dimensional computable incidence structure makes the carrier easy by hardwiring basis parities. This is a new concrete falsifier for the source lower bound, while the polylog-query target bridge remains valid. units.title: cycle-0053: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR carrier affine-incidence audit

Bad seeds cost EN gates to patch, and a sketch of total cost s+Kr+EN below N^{1+epsilon} is a concrete falsifier for the source lower bound. units.title: cycle-0054: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR Carrier Approximate Affine-Sketch Gate

units.content: Cycle 55 adds the SAT-preserving quotient normal form for XOR carriers. The valid target bridge is still max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, but the source lower bound must beat quotient piecewise-affine incidence sketches, not raw range or rank. Symmetry-pair cancellation is a concrete falsifier that can make a high-entropy generator compute a constant carrier; this is route-level progress only, not a proof of P != NP. units.title: cycle-0055: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 56 adds a sharper conservation law for XOR carriers: after SAT-preserving parity quotienting, H_N is easy whenever the incidence map has either low affine rank or a low-cardinality computable transcript, with patchable errors charged by EN. Thus high quotient entropy or high rank alone is not valid source evidence; the source obligation is a combined codebook-or-rank minimax lower bound, while the target bridge remains unchanged. units.title: cycle-0056: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR quotient codebook gate

units.content: Cycle 57 adds a nonlinear conservation law for the XOR carrier. The source lower bound must beat low-degree quotient-feature sketches with threshold S_T+binom(r,<=t)+EN, so high rank or high codebook entropy is not valid evidence. The target-preserving bridge is unchanged, but the source obligation is narrower and more nonrelativizing. Next: Formalize the degree-2 case: characterize whether Tseitin-style parity, formula-size, variable-incidence, or clause-type features give r=N^alpha with 2alpha<1+epsilon for the generated length-(log N)^d SAT queries.
units.title: cycle-0057: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR quotient carrier, low-degree feature-sketch gate

units.content: Cycle 58 repairs the XOR-carrier audit: low degree was the wrong nonlinear measure. The valid upper-bound falsifier is sparse quotient-polynomial support with threshold S_T+A_N r_N+E_N N<N^{1+epsilon}. This preserves the polylog-query target bridge but narrows the source obligation and exposes a new extraction gap: sparse-sketch hardness is not yet general-circuit hardness. Next: Formalize the weakest nontrivial extraction candidate: restrict arbitrary H_N circuits to circuits whose wires are invariant under SAT-preserving quotient symmetries, and test whether such invariant circuits collapse to sparse quotient-polynomial sketches with subthreshold loss.
units.title: cycle-0058: Hardness-magnification bridge via XOR carriers and sparse quotient-polynomial falsifiers

units.content: Cycle 59 identifies a conservation law for the XOR-carrier audit: unrestricted sparse quotient-polynomial hardness is not a simplification of the source lower bound, since T=H_N is an admissible one-bit quotient transcript. The valid contribution is a sharper quarantine: sparse sketches remain concrete upper-bound falsifiers, while any proof-relevant sketch lower bound now needs a named label-free transcript class plus a nonrelativizing extraction theorem. The main P != NP conjecture is untouched. Next: Formalize the local-linear incidence transcript class for the XOR SAT carrier and compute the minimum sparse F_2 support needed under a random-generator model, while auditing whether any extraction from arbitrary circuits to that class can avoid the planted-control relativization falsifier.
units.title: cycle-0059: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR carrier sparse-sketch audit

units.content: Cycle 60 separates two notions previously conflated. Sparse quotient-polynomial sketches are valid upper-bound falsifiers only when the transcript is constructively label-free; otherwise T_N=H_N collapses the audit. The target bridge max{rho,q}<1+epsilon survives, but sketch-hardness is not a source lower bound without a nonrelativizing extraction theorem or a direct C(H_N) lower bound. Next: Define the first concrete compiler class T^{inc-lin}: T_N(x)=B_N a_N(x) for explicit SAT-preserving quotient matrices B_N of row sparsity polylog N, then compute the minimum S_T+A_N r_N for representing H_N by sparse P_N in the high-q, d=2 regime.
units.title: cycle-0060: Constructive Label-Free Sketch Gate for XOR Magnification

units.content: Cycle 61 upgrades the XOR-carrier audit from vague label-free transcripts to a costed global-codebook normal form. The valid new contribution is an explicit upper-bound falsifier C(H_N)<=S_T+S_D+tildeO(U_N+A_Nr_N)+E_NN. This closes a leakage loophole in sparse quotient sketches, while exposing the exact remaining gap: absence of label-free sketches is not a general-circuit lower bound without a nonrelativizing extraction theorem. Next: Instantiate a candidate generator and compute U_N,A_N,r_N,E_N for its SAT-preserving quotient codebook; if the cost is subthreshold, quarantine that generator, otherwise formulate the exact extraction theorem it would require.
units.title: cycle-0061: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization

units.content: Cycle 62 adds a new fork: high incidence rank can make the XOR carrier lower-bound property large, so an efficient semantic certificate would be natural, while low rank is an upper-bound falsifier.
